EPC Gradient Matrix Preparation

This tutorial prepares the real-space electron-phonon coupling (EPC) gradients using prep_mode: grad-epc in QTrans. OpenMX aluminum (Al) is the main example; the following sections explain the changes for collinear magnetic iron (Fe) and for Al using ABACUS.

The workflow has three stages: generate unperturbed and displaced supercells, obtain their electronic graph data, and construct the gradient matrices. For DFT settings and matrix extraction, see Generation of Hamiltonian and Overlap Matrices and the official OpenMX and ABACUS documentation.

Paths are relative to the tutorial repository root. Update installation and pseudopotential paths in all YAML files before running. Each case includes previously generated outputs in ref/ for comparison. Complete QTrans YAML configurations are shown below; replace /path/to/... with your installation paths. Parameters not specified in these files use the program defaults.

1. OpenMX: Al as the main example

The example is in tutorials/Al/openmx/epc-prep/. It contains Al-pri.vasp, input_epc_1.yaml, and input_epc_2.yaml.

Step 1. Generate the supercell structures

The first configuration generates structures without constructing gradients. The complete input_epc_1.yaml is:

basic:
  prep_mode: 'grad-epc'
  outdir: './'

software_path:
  openmx_read_path: /path/to/read_openmx
  openmx_dftdata_dir: /path/to/DFT_DATA19
material:
  struct_path: ./Al-pri.vasp
  nao_max: 14
  DFT_software: openmx

grad_epc:
  epc_sc_matrix: [3, 3, 3]

Leave grad_epc.graph_data_sc_path unset in this first stage. struct_path supplies the primitive-cell structure; this example uses POSCAR format. nao_max must match the orbital basis used for the electronic calculations.

epc_sc_matrix specifies positive odd supercell multipliers. Without an explicit size, QTrans determines it from epc_sc_auto_length. Here we use [3, 3, 3] as a quick tutorial example. Converge the supercell size for your system, taking account of the orbital cutoff radii listed in Atomic Orbital Basis Definition.

From the tutorial repository root, run:

cd tutorials/Al/openmx/epc-prep/
QTrans_prep --config input_epc_1.yaml > grad_epc_1.out

The calculation writes QT.UNITCELL in POSCAR format. If std_symm_cell is enabled, this is the standardized primitive cell; use a consistent reference cell throughout subsequent phonon, electronic, and EPC calculations.

The perturb/ directory contains mat_info_sc.npy and four OpenMX inputs, QTepc-0.dat through QTepc-3.dat. In general, the workflow creates \(3N+1\) structures for \(N\) atoms in the unit cell: structure 0 is unperturbed, and the remaining structures displace each atom in a representative cell along x, y, and z. The displacement amplitude is set by epc_sc_disp (default: 0.01 angstrom).

Important

Review the generated DFT settings before running the supercells, especially the basis, pseudopotentials, k-point sampling, and SCF tolerance. Keep all settings identical across the displaced and unperturbed structures. Preserve the generated structure numbering and its matching mat_info_sc.npy.

Step 2. Run DFT and pack the supercell graphs

Use a separate calculation folder for each structure. For this one-atom Al cell, the following commands illustrate the sequence from epc-prep/:

cd perturb/
for i in 0 1 2 3; do
    mkdir -p "$i"
    cp "QTepc-${i}.dat" "$i/openmx.dat"
    (cd "$i" && mpirun -np 8 openmx openmx.dat > openmx.out)
done

The generated OpenMX inputs use System.Name QTrans. Therefore graph packing reads QTrans.scfout and QTrans.out in each calculation folder, rather than the crystal.* filenames in the unit-cell tutorial. Check that all four SCF calculations have converged.

Next, pack the supercell results into a single graph dataset. Create input_graph.yaml in perturb/ using the reference configuration at ref/perturb/input_graph.yaml as a guide:

basic:
  prep_mode: 'graph-pack'
  outdir: './'

software_path:
  openmx_read_path: /path/to/read_openmx

material:
  nao_max: 14
  DFT_software: openmx

graph_pack:
  HSout_filename: 'QTrans.scfout'
  vbout_filename: 'QTrans.out'
  data_folder: ./*/
  converge_step_ratio: 0.9

From perturb/, run:

mpirun -np 4 QTrans_prep --config input_graph.yaml > graph.out
cd ..

Verify that all four folders were included. The output perturb/graph_data_QTrans.npz must contain the unperturbed structure followed by the three displaced structures in the original order. Missing or unconverged structures must be corrected before constructing gradients. See Generation of Hamiltonian and Overlap Matrices for graph-packing details.

Step 3. Construct the gradients

The second configuration reads the supercell graphs and mapping. In input_epc_2.yaml, use the following complete configuration:

basic:
  prep_mode: 'grad-epc'
  outdir: './'

software_path:
  openmx_pp_path: /path/to/openmx_postprocess
  openmx_read_path: /path/to/read_openmx
  openmx_dftdata_dir: /path/to/DFT_DATA19

material:
  struct_path: ./Al-pri.vasp
  nao_max: 14
  DFT_software: openmx

grad_epc:
  graph_data_sc_path: ./perturb/graph_data_QTrans.npz
  mat_info_sc_path: ./perturb/mat_info_sc.npy

Unlike structure generation, this stage requires openmx_postprocess as well as read_openmx. Obtain these tools from the HamGNN project. QTrans invokes these tools to compute the onsite overlap derivatives in dSon/; finite differences of the electronic Hamiltonian alone are not sufficient in a nonorthogonal atomic-orbital basis.

From tutorials/Al/openmx/epc-prep/, run with a single process:

QTrans_prep --config input_epc_2.yaml > grad_epc_2.out

Check for QTRANS JOB SUCCESS and compare the outputs with ref/. The resulting grad_mat.npy is the dense gradient matrix; grad_mat_sparse.npy is its sparse representation, controlled by grad_sparse_thr.

2. OpenMX: magnetic Fe

The Fe example is in tutorials/Fe/openmx/epc-prep/. Follow the Al sequence with Fe-pri.dat and the supplied input_epc_1.yaml and input_epc_2.yaml. The complete first configuration is:

basic:
  prep_mode: 'grad-epc'
  outdir: './'

software_path:
  openmx_dftdata_dir: /path/to/DFT_DATA19

material:
  struct_path: ./Fe-pri.dat
  nao_max: 14
  DFT_software: openmx
  magnetic_type: collinear

grad_epc:
  epc_sc_matrix: [3, 3, 3]

The OpenMX structure input carries magnetic information in addition to atomic positions. Use spin populations consistent with the converged reference magnetic state, rather than arbitrary initial guesses. The prepared supercells, SCF calculations, graph packing, and gradient construction must all describe the same collinear, no-SOC system. See the Fe discussion in Generation of Hamiltonian and Overlap Matrices.

From the tutorial repository root, start with:

cd tutorials/Fe/openmx/epc-prep/
QTrans_prep --config input_epc_1.yaml > grad_epc_1.out

Run the four generated OpenMX supercells as for Al. When packing them, include material.magnetic_type: collinear in input_graph.yaml; the reference file is ref/perturb/input_graph.yaml and uses converge_step_ratio: 0.95. It reads QTrans.scfout and QTrans.out from ./*/. Check that all four magnetic calculations are included.

The complete Fe perturb/input_graph.yaml is:

basic:
  prep_mode: 'graph-pack'
  outdir: './'

software_path:
  openmx_read_path: /path/to/read_openmx

material:
  nao_max: 14
  DFT_software: openmx
  magnetic_type: collinear

graph_pack:
  HSout_filename: 'QTrans.scfout'
  vbout_filename: 'QTrans.out'
  data_folder: ./*/
  converge_step_ratio: 0.95

The complete Fe input_epc_2.yaml is:

basic:
  prep_mode: 'grad-epc'
  outdir: './'

software_path:
  openmx_pp_path: /path/to/openmx_postprocess
  openmx_read_path: /path/to/read_openmx
  openmx_dftdata_dir: /path/to/DFT_DATA19

material:
  struct_path: ./Fe-pri.dat
  nao_max: 14
  DFT_software: openmx
  magnetic_type: collinear

grad_epc:
  epc_sc_matrix: [3, 3, 3]
  graph_data_sc_path: ./perturb/graph_data_QTrans.npz
  mat_info_sc_path: ./perturb/mat_info_sc.npy

Then, from epc-prep/, run:

QTrans_prep --config input_epc_2.yaml > grad_epc_2.out

The second configuration supplies ./perturb/graph_data_QTrans.npz and ./perturb/mat_info_sc.npy, just as for Al. Compare the dense and sparse gradient outputs and logs with ref/. Keep the collinear magnetic setting when using these datasets in subsequent calculations.

3. ABACUS: Al

The ABACUS example is in tutorials/Al/abacus/epc-prep/. The workflow remains structure generation, DFT and graph packing, then gradient construction. Use the supplied STRU instead of Al-pri.vasp, because it contains the structure, species, and orbital-file information for ABACUS.

Step 1. Generate ABACUS supercells

Update the executable and data-directory paths in both preparation files. The complete input_epc_1.yaml is:

basic:
  prep_mode: 'grad-epc'
  outdir: './'

software_path:
  abacus_pp_path: /path/to/abacus
  abacus_dftdata_dir: /path/to/SG15_ONCV
  abacus_orb_dir: /path/to/SG15-std

material:
  nao_max: 40
  DFT_software: abacus
  struct_path: ./STRU

grad_epc:
  epc_sc_matrix: [3, 3, 3]

From the tutorial repository root, run:

cd tutorials/Al/abacus/epc-prep/
QTrans_prep --config input_epc_1.yaml > grad_epc_1.out

The generated perturb/QTepc-0.dat through QTepc-3.dat are ABACUS STRU files despite their .dat extension. Keep the accompanying mat_info_sc.npy for the final stage.

Step 2. Run ABACUS and pack the graphs

Place each generated structure in its own numbered directory as STRU. Provide matching INPUT and KPT files; reference templates are in ref/perturb/. Update their pseudopotential and orbital paths and retain basis_type lcao, calculation scf, suffix Al, and out_mat_hs2 1. With these files prepared in perturb/, run:

cd perturb/
for i in 0 1 2 3; do
    mkdir -p "$i"
    cp "QTepc-${i}.dat" "$i/STRU"
    cp INPUT KPT "$i/"
    (cd "$i" && mpirun -np 16 abacus > abacus.out)
done

Check convergence and the matrix outputs in each OUT.Al/ directory. The reference graph-packing configuration is ref/perturb/input.yaml. The complete perturb/input.yaml for graph packing is shown below. Update its software paths before running:

basic:
  # prep_mode: 'grad-epc'
  prep_mode: 'graph-pack'
  outdir: './'

software_path:
  abacus_pp_path: /path/to/abacus
  abacus_dftdata_dir: /path/to/SG15_ONCV
  abacus_orb_dir: /path/to/SG15-std

material:
  nao_max: 40
  DFT_software: abacus
  # magnetic_type: collinear
  # struct_path: /path/to/STRU

graph_pack:
  data_folder: ./*/
  abacus_out_folder: OUT.Al
  abacus_scf_log: running_scf.log

grad_epc:
  epc_sc_matrix: [3, 3, 3]
  # fd_method: central

Run from perturb/:

mpirun -np 4 QTrans_prep --config input.yaml > pack.out
cd ..

Verify that all four supercells were packed in the original order. Compare with ref/perturb/pack.out and ref/perturb/graph_data_QTrans.npz.

Step 3. Construct the ABACUS gradients

The supplied input_epc_2.yaml reads the same graph and mapping paths as the OpenMX examples. Its complete contents are:

basic:
  prep_mode: 'grad-epc'
  outdir: './'

software_path:
  abacus_pp_path: /path/to/abacus
  abacus_dftdata_dir: /path/to/SG15_ONCV
  abacus_orb_dir: /path/to/SG15-std

material:
  nao_max: 40
  DFT_software: abacus
  struct_path: ./STRU

grad_epc:
  graph_data_sc_path: ./perturb/graph_data_QTrans.npz
  mat_info_sc_path: ./perturb/mat_info_sc.npy

Keep DFT_software: abacus, nao_max: 40, and struct_path: ./STRU. The abacus_pp_path executable is invoked during the onsite-overlap calculation in dSon/; use an executable compatible with this step and ensure the configured pseudopotential and orbital files are available. This example supplies the ABACUS executable through that parameter.

Run from tutorials/Al/abacus/epc-prep/:

QTrans_prep --config input_epc_2.yaml > grad_epc_2.out

The outputs are grad_mat.npy and grad_mat_sparse.npy. Compare the completion log and matrices with ref/grad_epc_2.out and the reference matrix files.

Using the prepared data

In the calculator configuration, set epc.grad_mat_path to the selected gradient file and epc.mat_info_sc_path to its matching mapping. Use advanced.read_sparse_grad_mat: True with grad_mat_sparse.npy and False with grad_mat.npy. The electronic unit-cell data, phonon reference cell, basis, magnetic settings, and gradients must be consistent.

For OpenMX Al, the generated files are handed to the calculation tutorials as follows (paths are relative to the tutorial repository root):

Generated file under tutorials/Al/openmx/

Destination under the same directory

Calculator input key

graph-pack/graph_data_QTrans.npz

data/graph_data.npz

basic.graph_data_path_uc

epc-prep/grad_mat.npy or epc-prep/grad_mat_sparse.npy

data/grad_mat.npy or data/grad_mat_sparse.npy

epc.grad_mat_path

epc-prep/perturb/mat_info_sc.npy

data/mat_info_sc.npy

epc.mat_info_sc_path

After successfully generating the gradients, run from the tutorial repository root:

cp -i tutorials/Al/openmx/epc-prep/grad_mat.npy tutorials/Al/openmx/data/grad_mat.npy
cp -i tutorials/Al/openmx/epc-prep/grad_mat_sparse.npy tutorials/Al/openmx/data/grad_mat_sparse.npy
cp -i tutorials/Al/openmx/epc-prep/perturb/mat_info_sc.npy tutorials/Al/openmx/data/mat_info_sc.npy

The -i option asks before replacing supplied example data. Alternatively, keep all generated files in a separate directory and update the paths in the calculator YAML. Copy the matching mapping whenever the gradients are replaced; a mapping from another supercell preparation is not interchangeable. For OpenMX Fe or ABACUS Al, use the corresponding material/software paths and copy the outputs of that case rather than the Al/OpenMX files.

These steps do not prepare the phonon inputs. Follow Phonon Force Data Preparation for FORCE_SETS and its reference structure, and keep the phonon and EPC structures consistent. The complete calculator YAML files in the following tutorials show the final input paths.

If using predicted Hamiltonians instead of SCF Hamiltonians, set grad_epc.use_prediction: True and provide grad_epc.pred_H_sc_path together with matching supercell graph data. A unit-cell prediction alone cannot replace the full set of supercell predictions. See Generation of Hamiltonian and Overlap Matrices for the prediction workflow.

Note

Run grad-epc with a single process: its main preparation and gradient work is performed on rank 0. The separate graph-pack step supports MPI distribution across supercell folders, as illustrated above. MPI parallelism in the DFT commands is controlled by the external DFT code.
